threads.body: [General] Preserve the deprecated property's legacy matching semantics. This converts every legacy value into an `IncludeExclude` glob, but the old implementation treated entries as exact keys and recognized `*` as capture-all only when it was the sole entry (which the updated metadata also documents). For example, a legacy value of `request.*` will now unexpectedly capture `request.secret`, and `*,foo` will now capture every key; that is a compatibility and potential data-exposure regression. Keep exact-key/sole-`*` matching for the deprecated path and use glob matching only for the new selector properties.

Addressed in 004eed1bc1ea0d418d51c44c56ccbe7415675434.

Analysis: The deprecated configuration path was incorrectly converted to IncludeExclude glob matching. The selector now exposes a common predicate while retaining IncludeExclude matching for the new properties, exact set membership for deprecated keys, and select-all behavior only for a lone `*`.

Upsides: Preserves legacy compatibility, prevents wildcard-like key names from exposing additional MDC values, and adds focused coverage for `?`, embedded `*`, mixed `*`, and lone-`*` behavior.

Downsides: Introduces a predicate abstraction and one exact-key set allocation during mapper initialization.

replies.body: Removed the extra selector warning paragraph and declarative configuration snippet to keep this README consistent with the Log4j and Logback documentation.

Follow-up: after aligning the three logging selector changes, we decided to keep the declarative example for cross-instrumentation consistency. It now uses the complete valid `instrumentation/development` root, and the sensitive-data guidance applies to captured MDC attributes generally rather than only to exclude-only selectors.
